_note: Controller aim assist (src/game/aimassist.ts). The game does not publish its aim assist code, so these are its known settings where they are known and ours where they are not. Rotational strength 0.4 is the PC controller value Respawn has stated (console was 0.6 until Season 20 brought it to 0.4 too). The slowdown and the zone size are ours, chosen so a stick correction on a target does not overshoot without the pad tracking by itself. Mouse input is never assisted.
_levels: The strength a player picks (Settings, Controller; Milestone 620). Tiger, the fifth playtester, played on a controller and "barely noticed the aim assist" (the owner, 2026-10-12). light is what every pad had until then: Respawn's PC controller rotational 0.4 with our slowdown and zone. standard, the default now, is the console's 0.6 rotational from before Season 20, a deeper slowdown, a wider zone and the snap on aiming; strong goes further, for a player still learning the stick. rotational and rotationalAds: the share of the target's movement across the screen the view follows while you use a stick (hip and aimed); slowdownHip and slowdownAds: the look speed in the zone, 1 is none; zoneHip and zoneAds: the zone's radius round the chest, metres; snap: the share of the way to a target the view turns as you start to aim (0 is none). Ours, tuned on the playtest's word.
_rotational: While the stick or the movement keys are in use, the view follows this share of the target's own angular movement across the screen (its strafe, or yours around it). Zero input, zero assist: it never tracks on its own.
_rotationalMaxDeg: a larger jump in the target's bearing in one frame is a teleport or a respawn, not movement to follow
_zone: The zone is a sphere of this radius (metres) round the target's chest, so it covers less of the screen the further away the target is.
_maxRange: metres; no assist beyond this (60 until Milestone 620: SpeedKills' fights at a sprint open up wider than the legacy game's)
_falloff: metres: full strength (slowdown and rotation both) up to falloffStart, easing to none at maxRange, so a far target is the player's own aim (25 until Milestone 620)
_snap: Aiming down the sights (the aim button going down on a pad) with a target in sight within snapAngle degrees of the reticle and snapRange metres: the view turns the level's `snap` share of the way to its chest over snapTime seconds, eased (each frame a share of what is left), the target followed as it moves. Ours, after the aim snap console shooters give a pad; the legacy game has none.
_sticky: no snapping: once a target is held, the assist stays on it while it is still in its zone, even if another comes nearer the reticle; a new target needs the reticle to leave the old one's zone
